newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: More than 4,000 Sudanese flee war, famine.
newsitem.headline: More than 4,000 Sudanese flee war, famine.

text.p: More than 4,000 Sudanese refugees have arrived in neighbouring Ethiopia since November, fleeing civil war and famine, Ethiopia said on Wednesday.
The government Department of Refugees and Returnee Affairs said up to 4,128 Sudanese had arrived from southern Sudan and more could be on their way to the Horn of Africa country.
"The refugees are fleeing to escape civil strife, famine and mass destruction of residential areas, crop and livestock looting in the Blue Nile Region of Sudan," the department said in a statement.
It said the arrivals had been resettled at a temporary camp in Ethiopia's western Tongo district.
Southern Sudan is the theatre in a war between the country's mainly Christian and animist southerners and the Moslem Arabised northerners. The war has raged on since 1983.
The biggest southern guerrilla movement is the Southern Sudan People's Liberation (SPLA) led by John Garang.
The war has killed hundreds of thousands of people and driven many more into exile.
Ethiopia is home to thousands of Sudanese refugees.
